A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlexDepth work. All 38 pages in each version, including the complete supplementary material, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth-estimation experiments, architecture ablations, inference-speed measurements, and cross-dataset evaluations in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and the supplementary material, including benchmark performance, ablations, and hardware measurements.

M1.justification: The five-model FlexDepth family, Scale-Driven Decoder components, adaptive masking, two-stage training, PoseNet, and losses are unchanged in Section 3 and the supplementary descriptions.

E1.justification: Both versions retain KITTI and Cityscapes training/evaluation, Make3D and DDAD transfer evaluations, and the same dynamic-scene cases and encoder-pretraining comparisons.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding main-text and supplementary comparisons. Table 3 changes 'Lite-Mono-8m' to 'Lite-Mono-8M', identifying the same baseline with unchanged scores.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, input resolutions, training budgets, metrics, and speed-testing procedures match. Sections 4.6 and 6.7 retain the same median-scaling versus least-squares alignment and sparse versus improved ground-truth protocols.

E4.justification: The decoder and encoder ablations, static/dynamic-region analysis, Stage-2 versus fine-tuning control, feature visualizations, and qualitative case studies are all retained with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains Flex-X-Large Abs Rel of 0.093 on KITTI and 0.086 on Cityscapes; Tables 6 and 13 retain 0.063 under least-squares alignment with improved KITTI ground truth.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 and the supplementary threshold and channel-scaling definitions are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The claims about scalable efficiency, dynamic-scene robustness, decoder design, and zero-shot generalization retain their meaning and scope. Repairing the concluding sentence does not alter its scientific claim.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are unchanged, including the complementary roles of in-domain self-supervision and foundation models in Section 6.7. Section 5 retains the same indoor applicability limitation.

D1.justification: Optimizer, learning rates, schedules, batch sizes, hardware, training time, and supplementary implementation details match. The source-code address is unchanged; correcting 'avalible' to 'available' does not change access information.

R1.justification: The same 58 cited works and research positioning are retained. Changes to references 9, 16, 33, and 41 concern bibliographic metadata, capitalization, and DOI information rather than different works.

P1.justification: v3 corrects spelling, missing spaces, capitalization, and the incomplete final sentence of the conclusion, and updates existing bibliography entries and the arXiv stamp. Section order and narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Small caption and label edits affect Figure 3 and Tables 2, 3, 6, and 7. All 16 figures and 14 tables retain their content, structure, and placement; the figure images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves readability and reference completeness by repairing the conclusion's incomplete sentence, correcting text and caption errors, and expanding existing bibliographic entries. The scientific evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the quality gain is limited to editorial polish.
